messages.subject: Moving Window
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris and everyone!

I am trying to get AKDE home ranges for about 40 elephants with 20 years of 1 hr or 30 min GPS interval tracking data. I am interested in getting annual home ranges (every 365 days) for each elephant using a moving window in a nested for loop. Can you advise on how to create these moving windows. Also, do I need to resample my data to a fix a day or are the 1 hr or 30 min good to go?

Many thanks,
Nelson Mwangi.

messages.subject: Re: Moving Window
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nelson,

You do not need to resample the data in ctmm, which is the benefit of working with continuous-time models. In the past, some forum users have posted their code for doing moving window analyses: e.g., https://groups.google.com/g/ctmm-user/c/e470UCh12yg/m/ltUL8H6lAAAJ
If you search, there are a few more examples. I need to code up a function for this at some point.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Occurrence error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Brett,

Sorry about that. It was just a coding error that recent versions of R don't tolerate any longer. I think it should be fixed on GitHub now. If it isn't fixed, then please send me a minimal working example so that I can check for sure.

I can't tell for certain, but it looks like you are fitting errors without calibration data or a prior and have some locations with missing DOP values? Maybe the DOP values are only missing in the tracking data and not the calibration data? If the error estimates are important here, it might be worth fixing that with calibration data or a prior (covered in vignette('error') ).
By default, when DOP values are missing from certain locations, I give them their own location class (like NA-HDOP) and then assign them a very large DOP value of 100. But that doesn't seem to be sufficient here, and you probably need a prior/calibration on top of that.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: akde hard boundaries
messages.body_plain:
My post above has at least two issues that Chris helped me to correct. The code is working now and I am just posting a reply here should it be useful to someone in future.

My first mistake was that I did not supply the SP argument in pkde(). The shapefile is not carried over in the individual UDs and hence my population level UD was not adjusted for hard boundaries. I should have looked at ?pkde.

The code below shows how you can make a land mask (hard barrier) from bathymetry data.

library(raster)
# read in bathymetery raster
r = raster('./ibcso.tif')
# set cells above sea level to NA and others to 1. (i.e., the NA cells are areas where animals can't go).
r[r >= 0] <- NA
r[r < 0] <- 1
library(stars)
library(sf)
spdf = as_Spatial(st_as_sf(stars::st_as_stars(r),
                        as_points = F, merge = T))
raster::plot(spdf, col="red",border="green")

messages.subject: Re: error from outlie()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

There NA values in the Argos.semi.minor column that I assume came from negative eigenvalues in the estimated covariance matrix, and if so you would want to se those to zero instead of NA.

If fix the bug you found and improved the code from using circular errors only to using approximate error ellipses, though it hardly made a difference on the data you sent me. You can download the update from GitHub:  remotes::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm")

Best,
Chris
